ops.new_text:
We therefore benchmark four representation families for unsupervised SR-versus-AF
separation \rev{(sinus rhythm versus atrial fibrillation)}, with the controls the original
pipeline lacked. \rev{Because SR and AF differ by definition in the regularity of the
rhythm, it is expected that compact hand-crafted features and a large foundation model
both recover the split.
The ordering of the representations is therefore not the contribution.
What the benchmark adds is what the controls reveal and how the representations behave
under deployment stress.} Our contributions are modest and empirical\rev{:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] A chance-corrected, patient-grouped and significance-tested clustering
benchmark of raw, convolutional autoencoder (conv-AE), hand-crafted, and two frozen
foundation-model representations. Patient-grouped means that no patient appears in more
than one fold. Each representation is bounded by a supervised ceiling, the accuracy a
supervised probe reaches on the same features, and the comparison is shown stable across
the assumed number of clusters.
\item[(ii)] Two reproducible methodological cautions that explain the original project's
misleading numbers. Internal validity indices such as the silhouette, which are computed
without labels, reward the degenerate collapse. Feature scaling, the per-feature
transformation applied to a representation before clustering (Yeo-Johnson power,
standard, quantile or robust scaling), changes the result by a wide margin.
\item[(iii)] The behaviour of the representations under two independent deployment
stressors: heavy class imbalance, and federation across sites that differ in class
proportions (non-IID). The 16 hand-crafted features have the highest adjusted Rand index
(ARI) at a 9:1 SR:AF ratio and retain the largest share of their centralized ARI under
non-IID federation.
\item[(iv)] A generalization check on a MIT-BIH beat-morphology task, the data\-set the
closest prior benchmark omits.
\end{enumerate}
\end{revblock}
We do not propose a new method. \rev{The statements about foundation models concern
HuBERT-ECG and ECGFounder, the two evaluated here, and the
separability-versus-clusterability phenomenon is credited to prior work.}

ops.new_text:
\paragraph{MIT-BIH.} \rev{For generalization we used} the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database
\cite{mitbih2001,physionet2000}. \rev{Each annotated beat was segmented into a
$[-300, +250]$\,ms window around the R-peak across both leads, which gives the raw beat window
about 400 dimensions (Table~\ref{tab:mitbih}). We formed a balanced
normal-versus-premature-ventricular (N-vs-V) task of 3\,000 beats (1\,500 per class) from
47 records, with the record as the grouping unit, so that no record contributes beats to
more than one fold.} This is a morphology task and a deliberate contrast to the PTB-XL
rhythm task\rev{: the PTB-XL classes differ in the timing of the beats across a 10\,s
record, whereas the two MIT-BIH classes are defined on single beats and differ in beat
morphology. The MIT-BIH beats were clustered with the $k$-means, Ward agglomerative and
Gaussian-mixture clusterers described below.}

ops.rationale: Overfull line at 247--255: the first line of the raw-flattening item ends on 'moving-', and TeX does not hyphenate the part of a compound before its explicit hyphen, so a discretionary mov\-ing gives the line a break that fits; the wording is unchanged.
ops.new_text:
We compare four families on PTB-XL (Table~\ref{tab:main})\rev{:}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Raw flattening} reproduces the original pipeline: each lead \rev{was}
mov\-ing-average downsampled and all leads \rev{were} concatenated into one vector
($\sim$2000 dimensions). It carries amplitude and energy but no \rev{cross-record}
temporal alignment. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, 1000 samples by 12 leads. A
non-overlapping six-sample mean per lead left 166 samples per lead and a
1992-dimensional vector. This arm treats the sample amplitudes as the features and
imposes no clinical model on the signal. All twelve leads entered because the arm
reproduces the originating pipeline, which concatenated every lead.}
\item \textbf{Convolutional autoencoder} (conv-AE): a 1-D convolutional autoencoder
with a 32-unit bottleneck, trained to convergence with a validation split. This is a
properly specified reconstruction model, in contrast to the original collapsed dense
autoencoder. \rev{Input: all twelve leads, resampled to 12 by 2500 and z-scored per lead.
A reconstruction objective compresses whatever carries signal energy, which need not be
what separates the classes.}
\item \textbf{Hand-crafted} (16 features): RR-interval statistics and irregularity
\rev{(the standard deviation of the RR intervals (SDNN), the root mean square of successive
RR differences (RMSSD), the proportion of successive RR differences above \mbox{50\,ms}
(pNN50), the coefficient of variation, RR entropy and mean heart rate)}, P-wave
presence and amplitude, QRS width and amplitude, and beat-template consistency\rev{,
[GAP: one-clause definition of beat-template consistency, from the study's feature
extraction]} \cite{hrvstandards1996,dechazal2004}, extracted with NeuroKit2
\cite{neurokit2021}. \rev{Input: lead II alone, 1000 samples, reduced to a
16-dimensional single-precision vector. R-peak detection and wave delineation were
performed on that one lead. Lead II is the standard rhythm lead, on which RR regularity
and P-wave presence are read. Automated AF detection from a single short lead has been
benchmarked in a dedicated classification challenge \cite{clifford2017af}. A single-lead
definition also lets the feature logic, RR timing and beat morphology, be carried to the
two-lead MIT-BIH beats as the 21-dimensional beat-morphology set, where a twelve-lead
definition would not apply. The arm measures directly the AF signature, RR irregularity
together with P-wave absence.}
\item \textbf{Foundation embeddings} (frozen): mean-pooled hidden states of HuBERT-ECG
(768-d) \cite{hubertecg2024} and the 1024-d pooled features of ECGFounder
\cite{ecgfounder2024}, both used as fixed feature extractors with no fine-tuning.
\rev{Input: all twelve leads. HuBERT-ECG received the first \mbox{5\,s} at
\mbox{100\,Hz}, flattened lead-major into a 6000-sample vector. ECGFounder received the
full \mbox{10\,s} record resampled to 12 by 5000 for its \mbox{500\,Hz} input and
z-scored once over the whole array. Both lead sets are fixed by the published models,
which are defined on the complete twelve-lead record. The pretrained models supply a
fixed ECG feature space, and the question is whether that space places the rhythm
classes in separate regions.}
\end{itemize}

ops.new_text:
\rev{Six elements separate this study from the closest ECG foundation-model clustering
benchmark \cite{lookingbeyond2026}:}
\begin{revblock}
\begin{itemize}
\item A hand-crafted axis turns a comparison between foundation models into a comparison
between representation families.
\item A supervised ceiling on every representation, linear and non-linear, tells a space
that does not hold the label apart from one that holds it in the wrong geometry.
\item An out-of-fold test of that distinction shows that a discriminant fitted on other
patients raises HuBERT-ECG from 0.160 to 0.549 in held-out ARI.
\item A second dataset and a second task type, the MIT-BIH beat-mor\-phol\-ogy task, extend
the comparison to the database that benchmark omits.
\item Two cautions a practitioner can act on are stated with their evidence: the
degenerate silhouette, and the dependence of the result on feature scaling.
\item Two deployment stressors are measured with the cost of each representation beside
them, and under these stressors the balanced-data ordering stops being the useful answer.
\end{itemize}
\end{revblock}

ops.new_text:
\rev{For unsupervised arrhythmia structure in the ECG, the spread of ARI across
representations exceeded the spread across clustering algorithms with\-in each
representation that clustered well, and chance-corrected external evaluation was required
to see it. This held on the two tasks evaluated here: SR-versus-AF rhythm separation in
PTB-XL and N-vs-V beat morphology in MIT-BIH. On balanced PTB-XL data ECGFounder,
pretrained on more than ten million recordings \cite{ecgfounder2024}, leads. At a 9:1
SR:AF ratio, 16 interpretable hand-crafted features overtake it, and under simulated
federation across ten heterogeneous sites they are the more predictable of the two,
retaining 0.92 of their centralized ARI against 0.69 and never falling below 0.455 over the
ten site draws. On PTB-XL the raw and conv-AE pipelines sit at chance under all five
clusterers. Internal indices and feature scaling are not neutral and must be reported.
Whether these results hold for multi-class arrhythmia cohorts, for other foundation models
and for a real multi-institution federation is open.}
